title: Smart Routing for EV Charge Point Operators in Mega Cities: Case Study of Istanbul
summary: The paper addresses route planning for EV charge point operators who must visit 100 charging stations across Istanbul. It clusters stations geographically with K-means and uses a genetic algorithm to order the clusters, then combines intra-cluster and inter-cluster routes. The best reported configuration (5 clusters, 10 K-means iterations, GA mutation 0.10, 100 GA iterations) gives 308.49 km versus 417.53 km for the sequential reference, described by the authors as roughly 35% savings.

match_target.why: The user hint names this exact result, and it is the paper's central optimized distance. Reproducing it requires only K-means on 100 points plus a small GA over 5 cluster centers, so it is cheaper than reproducing the entire configuration sweep.

tolerance.why: Rule 4: the paper reports no std/CI for this value and total distance in km is an unbounded score, so use a 10% relative band.

requirements.stmt: Use a real dataset of 100 EV charging stations in Istanbul with latitude, longitude, and station name.
requirements.quote: A collection of 100 EV charging stations, each with latitude, longitude, and station name.

requirements.stmt: Combine latitude and longitude into coordinate pairs for spatial analysis and keep station names in a separate list.
requirements.quote: Latitude and longitude values were combined into coordinate pairs for spatial analysis.

requirements.stmt: Initialize K-means centroids randomly rather than using k-means++ by default, unless a documented deviation is reported.
requirements.quote: randomly selected centers; this process is completed iteratively by updating the centers

requirements.stmt: Assign each station to the nearest centroid using Euclidean distance.
requirements.quote: Assign each point to the nearest centroid using Euclidean distance as given in Equation 1

requirements.stmt: Update each centroid to the mean of its assigned stations and repeat assignment/update until convergence or the configured iteration limit.
requirements.quote: Repeat the assignment and update steps until convergence or a fixed iteration limit is reached.

requirements.stmt: Determine an intra-cluster route through the stations of each K-means cluster before global cluster ordering.
requirements.quote: route ←determine optimal route within point_list (e.g., using TSP)

requirements.stmt: Use the genetic algorithm to optimize the global order of K-means cluster centers, then concatenate the corresponding intra-cluster routes.
requirements.quote: the genetic algorithm was used to determine the shortest routes between clusters

requirements.stmt: Initialize the GA with random cluster-order chromosomes, evaluate fitness by total distance, select shorter routes, crossover, and mutate.
requirements.quote: Random sequences of clusters were generated to form initial candidate routes.

requirements.stmt: Support the four reported parameter configurations, including the target configuration with 5 clusters, 10 K-means iterations, GA mutation rate 0.10, and 100 GA iterations.
requirements.quote: Key parameters include the number of clusters, iteration count, mutation rate, and genetic algorithm iteration count.

requirements.stmt: Compute the reference route distance as the sum of Euclidean distances between consecutive stations in dataset order, and the optimized distance as the sum of intra-cluster and inter-cluster distances.
requirements.cite: Section 4.2, Comparison Between Reference Route and Optimized Route
requirements.quote: Reference Route Distance: Summation of Euclidean distances between consecutive data points in dataset order.

requirements.stmt: Compute improvement percentage with Eq. 3: (reference distance minus optimized distance) divided by reference distance, times 100.
requirements.quote: The evaluations were made by considering the given calculations, reference route and optimized route distances

requirements.stmt: Render K-means clusters in different colors and the final route as connecting lines, exporting an interactive HTML map.
requirements.quote: The final map was exported as an interactive HTML file for practical use by field operators.

requirements.stmt: Use Google Maps API and gmplot for mapping/visualization; do not treat Google road-network distance as the Table 4 optimization metric unless reproducing road-based duration separately.
requirements.quote: Google Maps API and the gmplot Python library were used for mapping and visualization.

requirements.stmt: Report total distance and total duration for each configuration; treat duration reproduction as secondary because the paper gives no duration formula.
